34.14: You must worship only me, [and] not worship any other god, because I, Yahweh, cannot endure any rivals.
34.15: Do not make peace agreements with [any group] that lives in that land. When they worship their gods and offer sacrifices to their gods, and they invite you to join them, do not join them. If [you join them], you will eat the food that they sacrifice to their gods, and [you will not be faithful to me. You will be like people who] commit adultery, [who are not being faithful to their spouses] .
34.16: If you take some of their women to be wives for your sons, and these women worship their own gods, they will persuade your sons also to worship their gods.
34.17: Do not pour melted metal into molds to make statues for you to worship.
34.18: [Each year], during the month [of/named] Abib, celebrate the Festival of Eating Bread Made Without Yeast. [During that festival], for seven days you must not eat bread made with yeast, as I commanded you, because it was in that month that you left Egypt.
34.19: Your firstborn sons and the firstborn [male] animals of your cattle and sheep [and goats] belong to me.
34.20: The firstborn of your [male] donkeys [also belong to me]. But you may buy them back by [offering to me] lambs [in their place]. If you do not do that, you must [kill these animals by] breaking their necks. You must also buy back your firstborn sons. You must bring an offering to me each time you come to [worship] me.
34.21: [Each week] you may work for six days, but on the seventh day you must rest. [Even] during the times when you plow [the ground] and harvest [your crops], you must rest [on the seventh day].
34.22: [Each year] celebrate the Harvest Festival, when you begin to harvest the first crop of wheat, and also celebrate the Festival of Living in Temporary Shelters, when you finish harvesting [the grain and fruit].
34.23: Three times each year all the men must come to worship me, Yahweh, the God of the Israeli people.
34.24: I will expel the people-groups that live in the land [where you will be], and I will cause your territory to become very large. As a result, no group will try to conquer your country if you come to worship me each year during those three festivals.
34.25: When you sacrifice an animal to me, do not offer with it bread that is made with yeast. And during the Passover Festival, when you sacrifice lambs, do not keep any of the meat until the next morning.
34.26: I am Yahweh God. You must bring to my Sacred Tent the first part of the grain that you harvest each year. When you kill a young animal/kid [either a lamb or a calf], do not [prepare to eat it by] boiling it in its mother’s milk.”
34.27: Yahweh also said to Moses/me, “Write down the words that I have told you. By giving you these commands, I have made a solemn agreement with you and with the [other] Israeli people.”
34.28: Moses/I was there [on the top of the mountain] with Yahweh for 40 days and nights. During that time he/I did not eat or drink anything . He/I engraved on the stone slabs the words of the Ten Commandments, [which were part of Yahweh’s] solemn agreement.
34.29: When Moses/I came back down the mountain, carrying in his/my hand the two stone slabs on which were written the Ten Commandments, his/my face was shining because he/I had been talking with Yahweh, but he/I did not know that his/my face was shining.
34.30: When Aaron and the [other] Israeli people saw Moses/me, they were amazed/surprised that his/my face was shining. So they were afraid to come near him/me.
34.31: But Moses/I called to them. Then Aaron and the other Israeli leaders came to him/me, and he/I talked with them.
34.32: Afterwards, all the other Israeli people came near, and he/I told them all the laws that Yahweh had given to him/me on Sinai Mountain.
34.33: When Moses/I finished talking to the people, he/I put a veil over his/my face.
34.34: But whenever Moses/I entered the Sacred Tent to talk with Yahweh, he/I removed the veil. When he/I came back out, he/I would always tell to the Israeli people everything that Yahweh had commanded him/me [to tell them].
34.35: The Israeli people would see that Moses’/my face was [still] shining. Then he/I would put the veil back on his/my face again until the next time that he/I went into [the Sacred Tent] to talk with Yahweh.

35.1: Moses/I gathered all the Israeli people together and said to them, “This is what Yahweh has commanded you to do:
35.2: [Each week] you may work for six days, but on the seventh day you must rest. It is a sacred day, dedicated to Yahweh. Anyone who does any work on the seventh day must be executed.
35.3: Do not [even] light a fire in your homes on days of rest.”
35.4: Moses/I also said to all the Israeli people, “This is [also] what Yahweh has commanded:
35.5: Make offerings to Yahweh. Everyone who wants to should bring to Yahweh an offering. [These are the things that they may offer]: Gold, silver, bronze,
35.6: fine white linen, blue or purple or red cloth, [cloth made from] goats’ hair,
35.7: rams’ skins that are ◄tanned/dyed red►, fine leather made from goatskins, wood from acacia [trees],
35.8: oil for the lamps, spices to put in the olive oil for anointing and in the sweet-smelling incense,
35.9: [valuable] onyx stones or [other] valuable stones to fasten onto the [priest’s] sacred apron and put on his sacred chest pouch.
35.10: “All the skilled workers among you should come and make all the things that Yahweh has commanded:
35.11: The Sacred Tent and its covering, its fasteners and its frames, its crossbars, its posts, its bases,
35.12: the sacred chest with its poles and its lid, the curtain that will separate the Holy Place from the Very Holy Place,
35.13: the table with the poles [for carrying it] and all the things that will be used with the table, the sacred bread that will be offered to God,
35.14: the lampstand for the lamps with all the things that will be used to take care of them, the oil for the lamps,
35.15: the altar for [burning] incense, and the poles [for carrying that altar], the oil for anointing and the sweet-smelling incense, the curtain for the entrance of the Sacred Tent,
35.16: the altar for offering [sacrifices that will be completely] burned and its bronze grating, the poles [for carrying] that altar and all the things that will be used with it, the washbasin and its base,
35.17: the curtains [to surround] the courtyard and the posts and bases [for the posts from which to hang the curtains], the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard,
35.18: the pegs and ropes for the Sacred Tent and for the courtyard,
35.19: and the beautiful clothes that Aaron and his sons are to wear when they do their work in the Holy Place.”
35.20: Then all the Israeli people returned [to their tents].
35.21: Everyone who wanted to brought an offering to Yahweh. They brought some of the things that would be used to make the Sacred Tent and all the other items that would be used in the rituals, and the materials to make the sacred clothes [for the priests].
35.22: All the men and women who wanted to brought gold ornaments, earrings, rings, necklaces, and many other kinds of things made of gold, and they dedicated them to Yahweh.
35.23: And many people who had blue, purple, or red cloth or fine white linen or cloth made from goats’ hair or rams’ skins that were ◄tanned/dyed red► or leather made from goatskins brought some of these things.
35.24: All those who had silver or bronze brought them as offerings to Yahweh. All those who had some acacia wood that could be used for any of the work brought it.
35.25: All the women who were skilled to make cloth brought fine linen thread and blue, purple, or red yarn/thread that they had made/spun.
35.26: And all the women who wanted to made/spun thread from goats’ hair.
35.27: All the leaders brought valuable onyx stones and other valuable stones to be fastened to Aaron’s sacred apron and his sacred chest pouch.
35.28: They also brought spices [to put in the sweet-smelling incense], and they brought olive oil for the lamps and for the oil for anointing and for putting in the sweet-smelling incense.
35.29: All the Israeli men and women who wanted to brought these things to offer them to Yahweh, for doing the work that he had commanded Moses/me to do.
35.30: Moses/I said to the Israeli people, “Listen carefully. Yahweh has chosen Bezalel, the son of Uri and grandson of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
35.31: Yahweh has enabled his Spirit to completely control Bezalel and has given him ability and enabled him to know how to do very skilled work.
35.32: He can engrave skillful designs in gold, silver, and bronze.
35.33: He can cut ◄jewels/valuable stones► and enclose them [in tiny gold frames]. He can carve things from wood and do other skilled work.
35.34: Yahweh has also given to him and to Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach their skills to others.
35.35: He has given to them the ability to do all kinds of work that is done by craftsmen—those who create artistic things, those who make fine white linen, those who embroider designs using blue or purple or red yarn/thread, and those who make other cloth. They are able to do many kinds of skillful work.

36.1: “Bezalel and Oholiab, and all the other men to whom Yahweh has given ability and enabled them to understand how to do all the work to make the Sacred Tent, must make everything just as Yahweh has commanded.”
36.2: So Moses/I summoned Bezalel and Oholiab and all the other skilled men to whom Yahweh had given special ability and who wanted to do some of the work.
36.3: Moses/I gave them all the things that the people had brought as offerings to Yahweh for making the Sacred Tent. But the people continued bringing more things every morning.
36.4: As a result, the skilled men who were doing various things to make the Sacred Tent came to Moses/me
36.5: and said, “The people are bringing more than we need to do the work that Yahweh has commanded us!”
36.6: So Moses/I gave the skilled men this message that was proclaimed throughout the camp: “No one should bring anything more as an offering to make the Sacred Tent!” When the people [heard that], they did not bring anything more.
36.7: What they had already brought was enough to do all the work. [In fact], it was more than was needed!
36.8: All the most skilled men among the workmen made the Sacred Tent. They made it from ten strips of fine linen, and carefully embroidered it using blue, purple, and red yarn/thread to make figures that resembled the winged creatures.
36.9: Each strip was ◄14 yards/twelve meters► long and ◄2 yards/1.8 meters► wide.
36.10: They sewed five strips together to make one set, and they sewed the other five strips together to make the other set.
36.11: For each set, they made loops of blue [cloth] and fastened them on the outer edge of the strip, at the end of each set.
36.12: They put 50 loops on the edge of the first set, and 50 loops on the edge of the second set.
36.13: They made 50 gold clasps/fasteners, to fasten both of the sets together. In that way, the inside of the Sacred Tent was [as though it was] one piece.
36.14: They made a cover for the Sacred Tent from eleven pieces of cloth made from goats’ hair.
36.15: Each piece of cloth was ◄15 yards/13.5 meters► long and ◄2 yards/1.8 meters► wide.
36.16: They sewed five of these pieces of cloth together to make one set, and they sewed the other six pieces of cloth together to make another set.
36.17: They made 100 loops [of blue cloth]. They fastened 50 of them to the outer edge of the one set and they fastened 50 to the outer edge of the other set.
36.18: They made 50 bronze clasps/fasteners and joined the two sets together with them. In that way it formed one cover.
36.19: They made two more covers for the Sacred Tent. They made one from rams’ skins that had been ◄tanned/dyed red►, and they made the top cover from goatskin leather.
36.20: They made [48] frames from acacia wood and set them up [to support the covers for the Sacred Tent].
36.21: Each frame was ◄15 feet/4.5 meters► long and ◄27 in./66 cm.► wide.
36.22: They made two projections at the bottom of each frame. These were for fastening the frames to the bases underneath them. Each frame had these projections.
36.23: The skilled workmen made twenty frames for the south side of the Sacred Tent.
36.24: They made 40 silver bases to go underneath them. Two bases went under each frame. The projections on each frame fit into these bases.
36.25: [Similarly], they made 20 frames for the north side of the Sacred Tent.
36.26: They made 40 silver bases for them also, with two bases for under each frame.
36.27: For the rear of the Sacred Tent, on the west side, they made six frames.
36.28: They also made two extra frames, one for each corner of the rear of the Sacred Tent, [to provide extra support].
36.29: The two corner frames were joined from the bottom to the top (OR, joined at both the bottom and the top). At the top of each of the two corner frames they fastened a gold ring for holding the crossbar.
36.30: In that way, [for the rear of the Sacred Tent] there were eight frames, and there were 16 bases, two bases under each frame.
36.31: The workmen made 15 crossbars from acacia wood.
36.32: Five of them were for the frames on the north side of the Sacred Tent, five for the south side, and five for the frames at the rear of the Sacred Tent, the west side.
36.33: The crossbars on the north, south, and west sides of the Sacred Tent were fastened to the middle of the frames. The two long crossbars extended from one end of the Sacred Tent to the other, and the crossbar on the west side extended from one side of the Sacred Tent to the other side.
36.34: The workmen covered the frames with gold and fastened gold rings to the poles. The crossbars [were put] into the rings. The crossbars were [also] covered with gold.
36.35: They made a curtain from fine white linen. Skilled craftsmen embroidered it with blue, purple, and red yarn/thread, making designs [that resembled] the winged creatures.
36.36: They suspended/hung the curtain from four posts that were made from acacia [wood] and covered with gold. They set [each] post in a silver base.
36.37: They made a curtain to [cover] the entrance of the Sacred Tent. They made it from fine linen, and a skilled weaver embroidered it with blue, purple, and red yarn/thread.
36.38: [To support this curtain], they also made five posts from acacia wood and fastened gold clasps/fasteners to them. They completely covered the posts with gold. They also made a bronze base for each of those posts.

37.1: Then Bezalel made the [sacred] chest from acacia wood. It was ◄45 in./110 cm.► long, ◄27 in./66 cm.► wide, and ◄27 in./66 cm.► high.
37.2: He covered it with pure gold inside and outside the chest, and he made a gold border around the top of it.
37.3: He made/cast four rings from gold [and fastened them] to the legs of the chest. He put two rings on each side of the chest.
37.4: He made [two] poles from acacia wood, and covered them with gold.
37.5: He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the chest, in order that the chest could be carried [by means of the poles].
37.6: He made a lid for the chest. That was [the place where Yahweh would] forgive people’s sins. It [also] was ◄45 in./110 cm.► long and ◄27 in./66 cm.► wide.
37.7: He made two winged creatures from hammered gold.
37.8: One of these was put at each end of the chest. The gold [with which they were made] was joined to the gold from which the lid [was made].
37.9: [He placed] the winged creatures facing each other so that their wings touched each other and spread out over the lid.
37.10: Bezalel made a table from acacia wood. It was ◄36 in./88 cm.► long, ◄18 in./44 cm.► wide, and ◄27 in./66 cm.► high.
37.11: He covered it with pure gold, and he put a gold border around it.
37.12: He made a rim all around it, ◄3 in./7 cm.► wide. He put a gold border around the rim.
37.13: He made/cast four rings from gold and fastened the rings to the four corners of the table, one ring close to each leg [of the table].
37.14: The rings were fastened to the table near the rim.
37.15: He made two poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold. These poles for carrying the table were then inserted into the rings.
37.16: He also made from pure gold all the things to be put on the table. He made the plates, the cups, and the jars and bowls to be used [when the priests] poured out wine [as an offering to Yahweh].
37.17: [He] made the lampstand from pure gold. Its base and its shaft were hammered from [one large lump of] gold. [The branches of the lampstand], the cups for holding the oil, the flower buds and the petals [that decorated the branches of the lamp, the base, and the shaft were all hammered from] one [big] lump of gold.
37.18: There were six branches on the lampstand, three on each side [of the shaft].
37.19: Each of the branches had on it three [gold decorations that looked like] almond blossoms. These decorations also had flower buds and [flower] petals.
37.20: On the [shaft of the] lampstand there were four [gold decorations that also looked like] almond blossoms, each one with flower buds and [flower] petals.
37.21: On each side, beneath and extending from each of the branches, there was one [flower] bud.
37.22: All these [flower] buds and branches, along with the shaft, were hammered from one large lump of pure gold.
37.23: Bezalel also made seven small cups [for holding oil. He put one cup on top of the shaft and he put the others on top of the branches]. He made from pure gold the tongs [for removing the burned wicks] and the trays [in which to put the burned wicks].
37.24: He used ◄75 pounds/35 kg.► of pure gold to make the lampstand and all the things that were used to take care of it.
37.25: From acacia wood, Bezalel made the altar [for burning] incense. It was square, ◄18 in./45 cm.► on each side. It was ◄3 ft./90 cm.► high. He made [a projection that looked like] a horn on each of the top corners. The projections were carved from the same block of wood that the altar was made of.
37.26: He covered the top and the four sides, including the projections, with pure gold. He put a gold border around the altar, [near the top].
37.27: He made two gold rings for carrying the altar. Then he attached them to the altar below the border, one on each side of the altar. The poles by means of which the altar was to be carried were to be inserted into those rings.
37.28: He made those [two] poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold.
37.29: He also made the sacred oil for anointing and the pure sweet-smelling incense. He mixed the incense together as a skilled perfumer would.

38.1: [Several men helped] Bezalel to make the altar for burning sacrifices. They made it from acacia wood. It was square, ◄7-1/2 feet/2.2 meters► on each side, and it was ◄4-1/2 feet/1.3 meters► high.
38.2: They made [a projection that looked like] a horn on each of the top corners. The projections were carved from the same block of wood that the altar [was made of]. They covered the whole altar with bronze.
38.3: They made the pans in which to put the greasy ashes [from the animal sacrifices]. They also made the shovels for cleaning out the ashes. They made the basins and forks for turning the meat as it cooked, and buckets for carrying hot coals/ashes. All of those things were made from bronze.
38.4: They also made a bronze grating to hold the wood and burning coals. They put the grating under the rim that went around the altar. [They] made it so that it was [inside the altar], halfway down.
38.5: They made bronze rings in which to put the poles [for carrying the altar], and fastened one of them to each of the corners of the altar.
38.6: They made the poles from acacia wood and covered them with bronze.
38.7: They put the poles through the rings on each side of the altar. The poles were for carrying the altar.
38.8: The altar was [hollow] like an empty box. It was made from boards [of acacia wood]. They made/cast the washbasin and its base from bronze. The bronze was from the mirrors that belonged to the women who worked at the entrance of the Sacred Tent.
38.9: [Around the Sacred Tent] Bezalel and his helpers made a courtyard. To form the courtyard, they made curtains of fine white linen. On the south side, the curtain was ◄150 feet/46 meters► long.
38.10: [To hang the curtain], they made 20 bronze posts and 20 bronze bases, [one for under each post]. [To fasten the curtains to] the posts, they made silver hooks, and [they made metal] rods [covered with] silver.
38.11: They made the same kind of curtains, posts, bases, and hooks for the north side of the courtyard.
38.12: On the west side [of the courtyard], they made a curtain ◄75 feet/23 meters► long. They also made ten posts on which to hang the curtains, and ten bases, with silver hooks and [metal] rods [covered with] silver.
38.13: On the east side, [where the entrance is], the courtyard was ◄75 feet/23 meters► wide.
38.14: On each side of the entrance, they made a curtain ◄22-1/2 feet/6.6 meters► wide. On each side they [were hung from] three posts, and one base was under each post.
38.16: All the curtains around the courtyard were made from fine white linen.
38.17: All the posts around the courtyard were made of bronze, but the tops were covered with silver. The posts were connected with [metal] rods [covered with] silver. The clasps/fasteners and hooks were made of silver.
38.18: For the entrance of the courtyard, they made a curtain from fine white linen, and a skilled weaver embroidered it with blue, purple, and red yarn/thread. The curtain was ◄30 feet/9 meters► long and ◄7-1/2 feet/2.3 meters► high, just like the other curtains around the courtyard.
38.19: All the curtains were made of fine white linen. They were supported by four posts, and [under each post] was a base made of bronze. All the posts around the courtyard were connected with [metal] rods [covered with] silver. The clasps/fasteners were made of silver, and the tops of the posts were covered with silver.
38.20: All the tent pegs to support the Sacred Tent and the curtains around the courtyard were made of bronze.
38.21: Here is a list of the amounts of metal used to make the Sacred Tent. Moses/I told [some men from] the tribe of Levi to [count all the materials used and] write down the amounts. Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest, supervised those men.
38.22: Bezalel the son of Uri and grandson of Hur made all the things that Yahweh commanded Moses/me to be made.
38.23: Bezalel’s helper was Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. Oholiab was a skilled engraver who made artistic things. He made fine white linen, and he embroidered designs using blue, purple, and red yarn/thread. He also made other cloth.
38.24: All the gold that was used to make the Sacred Tent weighed ◄2,195 pounds/1,000 kg.►. They used the official standard when they weighed the gold.
38.25: All the silver that the people contributed when the leaders ◄took the census/counted the men► weighed ◄7,500 pounds/3,400 kg.►. They also used the official standard when they weighed the silver.
38.26: All the men who were at least 20 years old were counted, and they each paid the required amount. That was a total of 603,550 men.
38.27: They used ◄75 pounds/34 kg.► of silver for making/casting each of the 100 bases to [put under the posts to support] the curtains of the Sacred Tent.
38.28: Bezalel [and his helpers] used the ◄50 pounds/30 kg.► of silver that was not used for the bases to make the rods and the hooks for the posts, and to cover the tops of the posts.
38.29: The bronze that the people contributed weighed ◄5,310 pounds/2,425 kg.►.
38.30: With the bronze, Bezalel and his helpers made the bases for under the posts at the entrance of the Sacred Tent. They also made the altar for burning sacrifices, the grating for it and the tools used with it,
38.31: the bases for the posts [that supported the curtains] that surrounded the courtyard and the bases for the entrance to the courtyard, and the pegs for the Sacred Tent and for [the curtains around] the courtyard.

39.1: Bezalel, Oholiab, and the other skilled workmen made the beautiful clothes for Aaron to wear while he did his work as a priest in the Holy Place. They made them from blue, purple, and red cloth, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses/me.
39.2: They made the sacred apron from fine white linen and from blue, purple, and red cloth.
39.3: They hammered some thin sheets of gold and cut them into thin strips which they embroidered into the fine linen and into the blue, purple, and red cloth.
39.4: The apron had two shoulder straps, to join the front part to the back part at the shoulders.
39.5: A carefully-woven sash, which was made from the same materials as the sacred apron, was [sewn] onto the sacred apron. This was made exactly as Yahweh had commanded Moses/me.
39.6: They cut two valuable onyx stones and enclosed them in a tiny gold frame, and a skilled gem-cutter engraved on the stones the names of the twelve sons of Jacob.
39.7: They fastened the stones to the shoulder straps of the sacred apron, to represent the twelve Israeli tribes, exactly as Yahweh had commanded Moses/me.
39.8: They made the sacred chest pouch. They made it of the same materials as the sacred apron and embroidered it in the same way.
39.9: It was square, and the material was folded double, so that it was ◄9 in./22 cm.► long and ◄9 in./22 cm.► wide.
39.10: They fastened four rows of valuable stones onto the pouch. In the first row, they put a [red] ruby, a [yellow] topaz, and a [red] garnet.
39.11: In the second row, they put a [green] emerald, a [blue] sapphire, and a [clear/white] diamond.
39.12: In the third row they put a [red] jacinth, a [white] agate, and a [purple] amethyst.
39.13: In the fourth row, they put a [yellow] beryl, a [red] carnelian, and a [green] jasper. They set each of the stones in tiny gold frames.
39.14: On each of the twelve stones they engraved the name of one of the sons of Jacob, to represent one of the twelve Israeli tribes.
39.15: They made two [chains] from pure gold and braided them like cords, to [attach] the sacred pouch [to the sacred apron].
39.16: They made two gold rings, and they attached them to the upper corners of the sacred pouch.
39.17: They fastened one end of each cord to one of the rings.
39.18: They fastened the other end of each cord to the two ◄settings/tiny frames► [that enclosed the stones]. Then they attached the sacred pouch to the shoulder straps of the sacred apron.
39.19: Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the lower corners of the sacred pouch, on the inside edges, next to the sacred apron.
39.20: They made two more gold rings and attached them to the lower part of the front of the shoulder straps, near to where [the shoulder straps] were joined [to the sacred apron], just above the carefully-woven sash/waistband.
39.21: They tied the rings on the sacred pouch to the rings on the sacred apron with a blue cord, so that the sacred pouch was above the sash/waistband and would not come loose from the sacred apron.
39.22: They made the robe that is to be worn underneath the priest’s sacred apron, using only blue [cloth].
39.23: It had an opening through which [the priest] would put his head. They sewed a border around this opening, to prevent the material from tearing.
39.24: At the lower edge on the robe, they fastened [decorations that resembled] pomegranate fruit. The decorations were [woven from] blue, purple, and red yarn/thread.
39.25: Between each of these decorations, they fastened a tiny bell made from pure gold, so there was a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, alternating all around the hem of the robe
39.26: for [Aaron to wear while] he did his work as a priest. They made all these things exactly as Yahweh had commanded Moses/me.
39.27: They wove long-sleeved tunics/gowns from fine white linen, for Aaron and his sons.
39.28: They also made a turban of fine linen [for Aaron to wear around his head]. They made the caps and the undershorts [for Aaron’s sons] from fine linen.
39.29: They made the embroidered sash/waistband [for Aaron] from fine linen and from blue, purple, and red cloth, and they embroidered designs on it using blue, purple, and red yarn/thread, exactly as Yahweh had commanded Moses/me.
39.30: They also made the tiny ornament of pure gold and had a skilled workman engrave on it the words, ‘Dedicated to Yahweh’.
39.31: They fastened this to the front of the turban by a blue cord, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses/me.
39.32: Finally they finished all the work to make the Sacred Tent. They brought to Moses/me all the things that they had made. They had made them exactly as Yahweh had commanded me.
39.33: They brought to him/me the Sacred Tent and all the things that were used with it: the hooks, the frames, the crossbars, the posts and their bases,
39.34: the coverings for the Sacred Tent that were made of tanned/dyed rams’ skins and goatskins, the curtains,
39.35: the sacred chest that contained the stone slabs [on which the commandments were written], the poles, the lid for the chest,
39.36: the table with all the things that were used with it, the sacred bread [that was offered] to God,
39.37: the lampstand made of pure gold and all its lamps and all the things that were to be used to take care of it, the oil for the lamps,
39.38: the golden altar [for burning incense], the oil for anointing, the sweet-smelling incense, the curtain for the entrance to the Sacred Tent,
39.39: the bronze altar [for burning sacrifices] and its bronze grating, the poles [for carrying] it, and all the other things that were used with it, the washbasin and its base,
39.40: the curtains [that surrounded] the courtyard, the posts and bases that supported them, the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard and its ropes, the tent pegs, and all the other things that would be used in the Sacred Tent,
39.41: the beautiful sacred clothes for Aaron to wear when he did his work in the Holy Place, and the special clothes for his sons to wear as they did their work as priests.
39.42: The Israeli people had done all this work exactly as Yahweh had commanded Moses/me.
39.43: Then Moses/I saw all the work that they had done. Truly, they had done everything exactly as Yahweh had commanded [that it should be done]. Then Moses/I [asked God to] bless them.

40.2: “On the first day of the first month next year, [tell the people to] set up the Sacred Tent.
40.3: Put inside it the sacred chest [that contains the stone slabs on which are engraved] the Ten Commandments, and hang the curtain in front of it.
40.4: Bring the table into the Sacred Tent, and place on it all the things that are to be used with it. Bring in the lampstand and fasten the lamps to it.
40.5: Put the gold altar for [burning] incense in front of the sacred chest, and set up the curtain at the entrance of the Sacred Tent.
40.6: Put the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the Sacred Tent.
40.7: Put the washbasin between the Sacred Tent and the altar, and fill it with water.
40.8: Hang the curtains that will surround the courtyard, and hang the curtain at its entrance.
40.9: Then take the oil for anointing, and anoint the Sacred Tent and everything that is in it, to ◄set it apart/dedicate it► to me. Then it will be holy/sacred.
40.10: Also anoint the altar for offering sacrifices that will be completely burned, and all the things that will be used with it, and set it apart. Then it also will be holy/sacred.
40.11: Also anoint the washbasin and its base, to set it apart.
40.12: Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Sacred Tent, and wash them [ritually] with water.
40.13: Then put on Aaron his sacred clothes to ◄set him apart/dedicate him►, in order that he can serve me as a priest.
40.14: Also bring his sons there. Put their sacred tunics/gowns on them
40.15: and anoint them just as you anointed their father, in order that they also may serve me by working as priests. By anointing them [and their descendants], you will cause them and their descendants to be priests throughout all coming generations.”
40.16: Moses/I did all these things exactly as Yahweh had commanded him/me.
40.17: On the first day of the first month of the next year (OR, second year [after they/we left Egypt]), the people set up the Sacred Tent.
40.18: Following Moses’/my instructions, they set up the Sacred Tent and its bases, set up the frames, attached the crossbars, and put up the posts [for the curtains].
40.19: Then they spread out the coverings over the Sacred Tent, exactly as Yahweh had commanded.
40.20: Then he/I took the two stone slabs [on which the commandments were written] and put them in the sacred chest. He/I put the carrying poles [in the rings] on the chest and put the lid on top of the chest.
40.21: Then he/I took the chest into [the Very Holy Place inside] the Sacred Tent and hung the curtain. In that way, he/I prevented the people who were outside from seeing the chest. He/I did all this exactly as Yahweh had commanded him/me.
40.22: He/I set the table inside the Sacred Tent, on the north side, outside the curtain.
40.23: He/I placed on the table the bread that was offered to Yahweh, exactly as Yahweh had commanded.
40.24: He/I set the lampstand inside the Sacred Tent, on the south side, opposite the table.
40.25: Then he/I fastened the lamps to the lampstand in Yahweh’s presence, exactly as Yahweh had commanded.
40.26: He/I set the golden altar for burning incense inside the Sacred Tent, in front of the curtain [that separated the Holy Place from the Very Holy Place],
40.27: and he/I burned some sweet-smelling incense on it, exactly as Yahweh had commanded him/me.
40.28: He/I hung the curtain at the entrance to the Sacred Tent.
40.29: At the entrance to the Sacred Tent, he/I set the altar for offering sacrifices that were to be burned completely. Then he/I offered on it the meat that was to be burned completely and the grain offering, exactly as Yahweh had commanded him/me.
40.30: He/I set the washbasin between the Sacred Tent and the [bronze] altar, and he/I filled the washbasin with water.
40.31: Every time Moses/I and Aaron and his sons went into the Sacred Tent or went to the altar, they/we washed their/our hands and feet [ritually], exactly as Yahweh had commanded Moses/me.
40.33: Following Moses’/my instructions, they hung the curtains that surrounded the courtyard and the altar, and they hung the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard. So Moses/I finished that work.
40.34: Then the [tall bright] cloud covered the Sacred Tent, and Yahweh’s ◄glory/brilliant light► filled the Sacred Tent.
40.35: Because that light was very bright, Moses/I was not able to enter the Sacred Tent.
40.36: From that day, whenever the Israeli people wanted to move to another place, they went only when the bright cloud rose from above the Sacred Tent.
40.37: If the cloud did not rise, they stayed where they were and did not go on until the cloud rose.
40.38: Wherever they traveled, the bright cloud that [indicated] Yahweh’s [presence] was above the Sacred Tent during the day, and a [bright] fire was inside the cloud at night, with the result that all the Israeli people could see it [at any time].
